method: Intel Pin + libdft64 byte-precise DTA; stdin tainted via libdft file-syscall hook (fd 0), taint of every store's VALUE checked at IPOINT_AFTER when its EA lands in canary_after
notes: libdft64 observed the SPATIAL violation: 20 out-of-bounds stride-4 u16 writes into canary_after (offsets +0..+76, pc=0x4034ca) in the vulnerable harness vs 0 in the patched control -- the OOB writes track the fix. But because the harness fixes sreg==dreg==0, the buggy loop READS s[i] and WRITES d[i] at the SAME overshooting addresses, so the 20 OOB writes store byteswaps of the untainted canary constants, not attacker stdin. Under sound byte-level data-flow the stored VALUES are therefore UNtainted (0/20); the address is a constant base + untainted loop index. regs file confirmed fully tainted (80/80 bytes), and the source->value drop was localised with -candbg probes (load at 0x4034aa reads untainted memory on the 20 OOB iterations). This precise negative diverges from microtaint's saved verdict (sink_value_tainted=true); microtaint over-approximates the OOB value taint for this sreg==dreg configuration. Cross-check: the 20 IN-BOUNDS byteswap stores (offsets +0..+76 of the regs file, same pc=0x4034ca) read the fully-tainted register file and libdft reports 20/20 value-tainted -> in-bounds under-taint = 0, confirming taint DOES propagate through the htons byteswap when the source is attacker-derived; the OOB negative is thus a true source property, not a propagation gap.
